newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM Hashimoto departs for U.S., Oceania visit.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM Hashimoto departs for U.S., Oceania visit.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto departed Tokyo on Thursday for the United States for talks with President Bill Clinton, the first stop in a three-nation trip that will also include Australia and New Zealand.

Clinton is expected to raise concerns about trade issues, including the resurgence of Japan's bilateral trade surplus and disputes over aviation and ports, and about Japan's overall economy during what U.S. officials said would be about a 2-1/2 hour meeting on Friday.

Hashimoto, relieved of a major headache with the successful end of the 18-week-long hostage crisis in Peru, told reporters he was expecting Clinton to talk trade, a dominant issue in past bilateral summits.
"I have an impression that the United States is shifting toward economic issues," Hashimoto told reporters before he departed.

The meeting, the two leaders' first since Clinton began his second term, is also expected to cover bilateral security issues, as well as the situation in China and North Korea, Japanese officials said.
Hashimoto is scheduled to visit Congress and deliver a speech at the National Press Club on Friday and meet Vice President Al Gore on Saturday.
On Saturday, Hashimoto is slated to fly to Australia and then will visit New Zealand through Wednesday before returning to Japan on May 1.
